Hi Sara —

Great to hear you want to push to staging. I attached our working MAP and a short network checklist to this thread. High level answers below and an initial mutual-action timeline attached (nova_map_v0.3.xlsx).

Quick answers:
- API keys: We can issue short-lived API keys scoped to a service account. For production-like tests you can use our CMK integration — we’ll need the KMS key ARN and the security contact. Keys will be delivered via a secure DocuSign link.
- Org setup: We will pre-create the org namespace once you confirm org name and billing contact. You’ll receive an org ID (format: rw-org-<shorthash>). For POC, create a service account with Developer role; for production we recommend ServiceAdmin + BillingViewer.
- IP allowlist: We require an allowlist for management plane traffic and recommend providing a /28 for app egress. Minimum list: management API (TCP 443) from your CIDRs; optional control-plane SSH for debugging (TCP 22) if requested. Full details in the attached checklist.
- VPC peering: We support AWS VPC peering (cross-account) and Transit Gateway. For peering we need your VPC ID, region, CIDR block, and a preferred peering window. Our suggested window: 2026-11-25 02:00–05:00 UTC for canary testing.

Next steps (high level):
1) You confirm network contact and provide VPC details and KMS ARN (owner: NovaHealth).
2) Our infra team creates org + service account (owner: Mina).
3) NovaHealth provides CIDRs and allowlist entries; Redwood issues API keys via DocuSign (owner: Security).
4) VPC peering scheduled and canary run (owner: Infra).

I’ve looped in Vivek (technical lead) and Marissa (your customer success/eng sponsor) to help with the checklist and SLAs.

Attachments: nova_map_v0.3.xlsx (MAP draft), rw_network_diagram.png

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC kickoff & MAP - network checklist and peering details

Sara, Mina —

Adding the technical checklist and an abbreviated peering spec so NovaHealth infra can validate prerequisites. See inline:

1) Firewall / Allowlist
  - Management plane (API): TCP 443 to our management endpoints: 52.23.45.100/32 and 52.23.45.101/32 (we will add your CIDRs on our side once you provide them).
  - Application egress: we recommend a /28 allocation for app egress; if you need fewer addresses we can support /29 with slightly constrained parallelism.
  - Health-check: outbound TCP 443 from your app subnets to our health endpoint (health.redwoodinference.com).

2) IAM / Service Accounts
  - Create service account: novahealth-poc-svc; assign Developer role (IAM policy: rw:invoke, rw:kvcache-read).
  - For peering automation, create an AWS role with a trust policy for our peering account id (111122223333) so we can create the peering connection on your behalf (optional).

3) VPC peering specifics
  - Required: VPC ID, region, primary CIDR, route table IDs for the subnets in the peering scope.
  - Recommended: tag the subnets with rw:poc=true to simplify routing rules.
  - Collision handling: if overlapping CIDRs exist we provide NAT-based alternatives, but that increases latency and cost.

4) Canary plan (brief)
  - 11/25 02:00–03:00 UTC: smoke tests (API auth, basic generation, KV cache warm)
  - 11/25 03:00–05:00 UTC: scaled throughput run (limited to 10% of expected peak)
  - Rollback criteria: any 5xx >1% for 10 minutes or latency >1.5s P95

I attached the network diagram for clarity. If you prefer, we can do the peering handshake during your Tue/Wed maintenance window next week.

-Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
